title: Volatility Targeting Is Trendy: How Trend Following Explains Alpha in Volatility-Managed Strategies
one_line: Volatility targeting beats buy-and-hold in equities mainly because of the leverage effect (prices fall when volatility rises); controlling for trend following removes about two-thirds of its alpha across 14 stock indices, and the effect is absent in bonds, commodities and FX.

findings.statement: Controlling for trend following cuts volatility-targeting alpha by about two-thirds (14 stock indices).
The leverage effect and trend link are equity-specific.

why.pattern: Volatility targeting in equities behaves like trend following (de-risks in falling, volatile markets).

reported_results.headline: ~2/3 of vol-targeting alpha is trend exposure.

tradable_edge: For our VOLATILITY_SIZING view: expect smoother results and smaller drawdowns, not a new edge; on ES it partly duplicates trend exposure.
angles: Compare vol-sized vs fixed size on every strategy (already in the sizing view)
data_fit: ES 1-min Dec 2013 → Sep 2026, NQ 1-min Jul 2021 → Sep 2026 (2024+ protected in the backtest project).
